thread.title: Stocks Up On Oil Prices, China Trade; Apple Cuts Output | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Up On Oil Prices, China Trade; Apple Cuts Output | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks jumped into firm early gains Wednesday as China trade talks continued, oil prices climbed above $50 and the Nasdaq, the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrials sought to advance their young uptrend to a 10th day.
X Intuitive Surgical ( IRSG ) sprung higher after raising its fourth-quarter revenue guidance. Chipmaker Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ) led an early rally among chip stocks, despite lowering its guidance and receiving an analyst price target cut. Apple ( AAPL ) stock gave up its early gains to trade lower after a report that the company would trim its iPhone production. Marijuana stock Canopy Growth ( CGC ) leapt after some positive Mad Money comments from Jim Cramer.
Boeing ( BA ) and Visa ( V ) drove the Dow Jones industrial average to an early 0.8% gain. The S&P 500 jumped 0.5%, and Nasdaq Composite climbed 0.6%.
Western Digital ( WDC ) and Micron Technology ( MU ) led both the Nasdaq and the S&P 500.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Stock Market Uptrend: Day 10 As the market's young uptrend approaches a crucial technical test, the Nasdaq is closest to that watermark while the Dow Jones industrial average lags. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 each begin Wednesday's session less than 2% from the underside of their 50-day moving averages. The Dow is 3% from its 50-day line.
A break above that level would put the Nasdaq above the 7,000 mark, and the S&P 500 above 2,600. This could shift those levels, as well as the index's 50-day moving averages, into areas of support, buoying the rally. If the 50-day lines become a level of resistance, they could act as a cap to hold back the rally's progress.
Key data is due out later today — with oil supplies at 10:30 a.m. ET and Federal Reserve minutes at 2 p.m. — which could influence the stock market. Fed Chair Jerome Powell is scheduled to participate in a forum in Washington, D.C., on Thursday.
Apple Cuts iPhone Output 20% Apple stock rose 0.2% early. A report in Japan's Nikkei Asian Review detailed requests from Apple to its suppliers that would reduce total iPhone production in the January-March quarter to between 40 million and 43 million units, about 20% below year-ago levels.
Apple stock is struggling to form a bottom to its three-month consolidation. Shares ended Tuesday up 6% from last Thursday's low, and 39% below their October high.
Shutdown: Day 18 The budget impasse between the White House and House Democrats continues to keep an estimated 800,000 workers idled with the shutdown's first pay day approaching on Friday. No deal before then would mean workers do not receive paychecks.
There has been no sign of progress in the talks. But President Trump tweeted positive comments on Tuesday , and stock futures reacted positively after Trump made his case for a national emergency at the southern border in a televised speech Tuesday night.
In China, trade negotiations between the U.S. and Beijing entered their third day. Data on Wednesday showed China's auto sales declined in 2018 for the first time in more than 20 years.
Markets in China and Japan nevertheless hammered out big gains, led by a 2.3% advance by Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index. Markets also rallied in Europe, with the top benchmarks in London, Paris and Frankfurt all up more than 1% in afternoon trade.
Cannabis Stocks: Canopy Vs. Tilray Canopy Growth jumped 4.4% in early trade, while peer Tilray ( TLRY ) dropped 2.4%. Jim Cramer touted Canopy as a buy and Tilray as a sell Tuesday night. Cramer favored Canopy's ownership structure over Tilray's, and said the company was better capitalized.
Canopy shares are trading just below their initial 30.85 opening price when the stock shifted from over-the-counter to the Big Board in May. The stock is 51% below its October high.
Oil Prices: WTI Tops $50 U.S. oil prices surged past the important $50 level early Wednesday, as West Texas Intermediate gained 3% to trade above $51 a barrel. Oil prices have gained for eight consecutive sessions, as production restraints agreed to by Russia and the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries took effect Jan. 1, and Saudi Arabia revealed plans to further curtail its output and exports . The Saudis said they intended to target $80 per barrel oil prices for Europe's Brent crude benchmark. Brent rose 2.6% to above $60 early Wednesday.
The $50 level for WTI marks a price point above which U.S. shale oil producers are considered broadly profitable. Below $50, market are seen as tight and shale oil producers often begin to alter spending or production plans.
Skyworks, Intuitive Surgical Climb Apple chip supplier Skyworks Solutions jumped nearly 5% higher. JPMorgan trimmed the stock's price target to 76, from 80 after Skyworks lowered its first-quarter earnings and revenue guidance late Tuesday. It reduced the range of earnings expectations about 5%, and cut back around 4% on the revenue side.
Management cited weakness across large smartphone customers, which would include Apple. Despite the near-term challenges, broader markets "tracked in-line with our prior outlook. In addition, cash flow generation continued to be strong, allowing us to return cash to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends," according to a company statement.
Skyworks stock has lost 43% in a nine-month decline.
Intuitive Surgical popped 2.9% higher after raising it fourth-quarter revenue outlook to $1.047 bil., vs. the $1.03 bil. consensus target. The company also said fourth quarter procedures using the da Vinci robotic surgical system increased 19% over year ago levels.
